name: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
indicators: High IN_PKTS and IN_BYTES in short FLOW_DURATION_MILLISECONDS
Sustained high SRC_TO_DST_AVG_THROUGHPUT across distributed source IPs
SYN / ACK flood flags in TCP_FLAGS or high-rate UDP datagram bursts
High flows_10s from distributed origins converging on target port
description: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) flood overwhelming network infrastructure or services across coordinated distributed nodes.
mitigation: Activate upstream BGP Anycast routing, rate-limit SYN and UDP packets at border firewall, and apply flow scrubbing.

name: Denial of Service (DoS)
indicators: Extremely high packet count IN_PKTS targeting port 80/443
Low packet payload sizes (NUM_PKTS_UP_TO_128_BYTES)
Anomalous flow duration with incomplete handshakes or resource starvation
description: Denial of Service (DoS) attack attempting to deplete host sockets, CPU, or memory buffers by flooding target ports.
mitigation: Enable TCP SYN cookies on target hosts, configure connection drop timeouts, and apply ingress rate limiting.

name: Port Scanning & Network Enumeration
indicators: High unique_ports_10s from a single source IP
Short flow durations with single SYN packets (IN_PKTS = 1, in_bytes < 100)
Zero or minimal OUT_BYTES (unresponsive or closed ports)
description: Reconnaissance scan probing multiple L4 destination ports to discover active daemons, listening services, and firewall configurations.
mitigation: Temporarily quarantine source IP at perimeter firewall, implement port knocking, and hide unused listening ports.

name: Network Discovery & Reconnaissance
indicators: High sweep rate across destination IPs on internal subnet
ICMP Echo, ARP sweeps, or non-standard probe protocols
Repeated discovery queries on DNS / NetBIOS / SMB
description: Network mapping activity sweeping subnet ranges to map network topology, active hosts, and routing infrastructure.
mitigation: Block external ICMP sweeps, segregate internal VLANs, and deploy network decoy honeypots.

name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
indicators: Atypical request lengths on Web application ports (80, 443)
Deviation from normal HTTP client traffic latent distribution
Repeated client submissions with script tag / DOM injection patterns
description: Injection of malicious client-side scripts targeting browser execution contexts of other application users.
mitigation: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, sanitize HTML context inputs, and configure WAF inspection.

name: Password Cracking & Credential Spraying
indicators: Sequential login attempts to web or authentication endpoints
Consistent small payload sizes (600-900 bytes) across multiple flows
Repeated connection attempts from single or coordinated sources to port 80/443
description: Automated password guessing, credential stuffing, or dictionary attacks targeting web authentication portals.
mitigation: Enforce account lockouts, deploy CAPTCHA after failed attempts, and mandate multi-factor authentication (MFA).

name: SQL & Command Injection
indicators: Anomalous HTTP payload sizes on Web application ports (80, 443)
Unusually high client request payload length compared to normal GET/POST requests
High Autoencoder feature error on IN_BYTES and LONGEST_FLOW_PKT
description: Infiltration of malicious code fragments (SQL Injection, OS command injection, LDAP injection) through application data inputs.
mitigation: Use parameterized queries, enforce strict input validation, and enable WAF signature matching.

name: Botnet Command & Control (C2)
indicators: Periodic small byte beacons on TLS/HTTPS or high ports (e.g. 8080)
Persistent keep-alive flows with anomalous latent manifold position
Repeated communication with non-standard external IP endpoints
description: Botnet agent establishing automated periodic command-and-control communication to receive instructions or exfiltrate state.
mitigation: Isolate the infected endpoint from the local network, inspect DNS logs for DGA domains, and terminate unauthorized sockets.

name: Authentication Brute Force
indicators: Rapid succession of flows to administrative ports (22 SSH, 3389 RDP, 21 FTP)
High IN_PKTS (> 30 pkts/flow) and IN_BYTES (> 5,000 bytes) during repeated handshakes
Short flow durations followed by repeated reconnection attempts
description: Automated dictionary attack or credential stuffing attempting to crack authentication credentials on network services.
mitigation: Enforce Fail2Ban or IP lockout thresholds, mandate MFA, and disable public password logins in favor of SSH keys.

name: Network Infiltration & Lateral Movement (Infilteration)
indicators: Unusual intra-subnet traffic between internal workstations
DNS tunneling or non-standard protocol encapsulation on UDP port 53
Anomalous client-server role reversal on internal IP addresses
description: Post-compromise network infiltration where an adversary moves laterally through internal systems to compromise internal infrastructure.
mitigation: Implement zero-trust network segmentation, audit internal East-West traffic, and isolate compromised internal endpoints.

name: Exploits & Vulnerability Exploitation
indicators: Extremely large payload transfers (mean IN_BYTES > 40,000 bytes)
Atypical TCP window size or out-of-order segment flags
High reconstruction MSE in application payload size features and LONGEST_FLOW_PKT
description: Transmission of structured malformed payloads targeting known application vulnerabilities (CVEs) or buffer overflows.
mitigation: Apply vendor security patches, deploy Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspection rules, and inspect host execution logs.

name: Protocol Fuzzing & Fuzzers
indicators: Randomized packet sizes across consecutive flows on routing or application ports (179 BGP, 80)
Unusual combinations of TCP flags and invalid header fields
High reconstruction error across both ingress and egress dimensions
description: Automated transmission of semi-random, boundary-testing payloads designed to uncover zero-day crash conditions and memory faults.
mitigation: Filter non-RFC compliant packets at the network layer and monitor service daemon health for memory faults.

name: Backdoor Access & Reverse Shell
indicators: Interactive typing pauses and prolonged connection durations on non-standard ports (8080)
High OUT_BYTES relative to low IN_BYTES on non-standard ports
Outbound connection initiated from internal server to unknown public IP
description: Unsanctioned remote access channel or reverse shell allowing external threat actors covert command execution inside the network.
mitigation: Enforce strict outbound egress firewall filtering, terminate unauthorized interactive sessions, and run memory rootkit scanners.

name: Generic Cryptographic & Protocol Violation
indicators: Anomalous packet structures on UDP port 53 or transport tunnels
Cipher collision or non-conforming protocol state transitions
Multi-dimensional deviation in latent manifold density
description: Generic protocol violations, block cipher attacks, or non-standard protocol encapsulations deviating from RFC specifications.
mitigation: Apply protocol strictness verification at border gateways and inspect encapsulated packet payloads.

name: Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) Interception
indicators: Inconsistent TTL values (MIN_TTL vs MAX_TTL)
Duplicated or conflicting flow records with altered MAC/IP bindings
High retransmission count (RETRANSMITTED_IN_BYTES) and altered DNS responses
description: Adversary positioning between communicating network entities via ARP spoofing, DNS cache poisoning, or rogue gateways.
mitigation: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI), enforce 802.1X port authentication, and mandate end-to-end TLS encryption.

name: Ransomware Propagation & Lateral Movement
indicators: Sudden surge in SMB (Port 445) or RPC traffic to internal endpoints
Rapid file transfer volume (high IN_BYTES and OUT_BYTES)
High latent Mahalanobis distance indicating deviation from baseline workstation behavior
description: Malicious automated encryption activity rapidly spreading across network shares and staging extortion payloads.
mitigation: Immediately isolate affected subnets, disable SMBv1/v2 across domain endpoints, and initiate immutable snapshot restoration.

name: Security Analysis & Automated Scanning
indicators: Automated security scanner signatures (Nessus, Nikto, OpenVAS)
Low packet count per flow with rapid successive endpoint probes
Anomalous combinations of probe port requests and web spidering
description: Automated vulnerability scanner or web crawler analyzing network attack surface, application headers, and exposed endpoints.
mitigation: Enforce web crawler restrictions via robots.txt/WAF, monitor administrative IP whitelists, and rate-limit scanner probes.

name: Data Exfiltration & Theft
indicators: Massive outward data volume (mean IN_BYTES > 1.5 MB per flow)
Sustained high SRC_TO_DST_AVG_THROUGHPUT over prolonged flow duration
Unusual transfer volume on storage, cloud, or covert tunneling channels
description: Unauthorized transfer of proprietary, credential, or sensitive data from internal systems to external recipient infrastructure.
mitigation: Block egress traffic to untrusted cloud services, enable Data Loss Prevention (DLP) proxies, and throttle unusual outbound flows.

name: Shellcode Injection & Execution
indicators: Precise binary packet size signatures matching exploit staging buffers (e.g. port 1347)
High latent Mahalanobis distance from clean flow profiles
Sudden connection initiation following an inbound buffer delivery
description: Raw machine code injected into process memory during exploitation to open command access or download secondary payloads.
mitigation: Enforce ASLR and DEP on target servers, terminate offending process tree, and audit memory segments.

name: Self-Propagating Network Worms
indicators: Massive rapid proliferation of outgoing connections to neighboring IPs on port 80/445
Identical flow sizes across dozens of target endpoints
High TCP_FLAGS indicating continuous automated connection attempts
description: Autonomous malicious payload replicating across local network subnets by exploiting unpatched network vulnerabilities.
mitigation: Quarantine the originating network segment, apply emergency zero-day firewall blocks, and inspect host processes.

name: Statistical NetFlow Anomaly
indicators: High hybrid score across Autoencoder and Latent Isolation Forest
Multi-dimensional deviation in packet length and duration distributions
Significant distance from benign topological baseline manifold
description: Multi-variate statistical anomaly significantly exceeding the calibrated normal baseline threshold across NetFlow dimensions.
mitigation: Review network flow details, verify host process integrity, and capture full packet PCAP for forensic inspection.
